title: Education Technology is Never Neutral
author: Daisy Christodoulou
summary: Christodoulou rejects the argument that technology is neutral, instead proposing that tools profoundly shape behavior and learning outcomes. She draws on Marshall McLuhan's "the medium is the message" and demonstrates that tools make certain behaviors more likely and others less so: an eraser changes classroom attitudes toward error; a screen prioritizes task-switching over deep focus. Mode effects research from 3,000+ students shows that paper-based assessment produces performance 20 scaled-score points higher than computer-based assessment—equivalent to six months of additional schooling. Christodoulou argues that tool selection represents true human agency: once a tool is chosen, its constraints are already in place. Different screen types (laptops, phones, tablets) are optimized for different functions and make those functions more likely. The article concludes that high-functioning organizations deliberatelychoose appropriate tools rather than treating technology as interchangeable, and that designers bear responsibility for ensuring tools make good outcomes more likely and poor outcomes less likely.
points: Tools are not neutral: they make certain behaviors more likely and constrain others, with more powerful tools creating narrower ranges of behavior.
Paper-based assessment outperforms computer-based assessment by 20 scaled-score points (equivalent to six months of schooling).
Different screen types (laptops, phones, tablets) are optimized for different functions, shaping what users are likely to do.
True agency lies in tool selection and design input, not in how tools are used once constraints are in place.
Well-functioning organizations deliberately choose tools fit for purpose rather than treating technology as neutral and interchangeable.
quotes: You don’t see people walking down the street texting on their laptop. And people tend not to write novels on their phones. Tablets are different again.
